title: PostgreSQL Connection Pool Exhaustion in User Auth Service
description: API Gateway began returning HTTP 500 Internal Server Errors on all /auth/login and /auth/refresh endpoints during peak morning traffic spike.
error_logs:
FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections (SQLSTATE 53300)
org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
at org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication
at pg_pool_client.acquire(connection.js:142)
TimeoutError: ResourceRequest timed out after 10000ms
root_cause: Node.js auth service leaked database connections during token refresh retry bursts due to missing release() in an unhandled promise rejection branch. PostgreSQL max_connections (100) was saturated with 'idle in transaction' handles.
steps_taken:
1. Executed 'SELECT count(*), state, usename FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state, usename;' revealing 97 idle in transaction connections from auth pods.
2. Identified client IPs belonging to auth-service deployment replicas.
3. Executed 'SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND state_change < now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';' to instantly restore DB availability.
4. Audited auth-service Knex pool config and connection release logic.
resolution: Configured PgBouncer transaction-level pooling with max_client_conn=1000 and default_pool_size=25. Capped microservice pool to max 10 connections with 5000ms idleTimeoutMillis, and released hotfix v2.4.1 fixing the dangling promise in token refresh.

title: Redis Out of Memory (OOM) Eviction Failure in Session Store
description: Users experienced unexpected logouts across the web dashboard. Writing new session keys failed across all web worker nodes.
error_logs:
Redis::CommandError: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
at SessionStore.set(session_store.rb:88)
at ActionDispatch::Session::RedisStore#set_session
Used memory: 8.00GB / 8.00GB (100% capacity). Eviction policy: volatile-lru
root_cause: Telemetry events were erroneously written to the session Redis instance without a TTL (Time-To-Live). Because eviction policy was volatile-lru, keys without expiry could not be evicted, choking all 8GB of memory.
steps_taken:
1. Inspected memory allocation using 'redis-cli --bigkeys' and 'redis-cli memory usage'.
2. Discovered 1.8M unexpired keys matching pattern 'telemetry:event:*'.
3. Executed non-blocking scan and unlink: 'redis-cli --scan --pattern 'telemetry:*' | xargs -L 500 redis-cli unlink'.
4. Verified memory drop from 8.0GB to 1.8GB.
resolution: Altered Redis maxmemory-policy to 'allkeys-lru' as a safeguard. Directed telemetry data exclusively to Kafka/ClickHouse and enforced strict 7-day TTL (EX 604800) in Redis helper.

title: Ingress TLS Certificate Expiration on Edge Gateway
description: Browser clients reported security warnings 'NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID' when connecting to public API endpoints.
error_logs:
nginx: [warn] certificate for api.example.com expired at 2026-10-15 00:00:00 GMT
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
Cert-Manager log: 'Failed to complete HTTP-01 challenge: 404 Not Found on /.well-known/acme-challenge/'
root_cause: A recent ingress routing update redirected all non-API routes to an SPA single-page application router, which intercepted and broke Let's Encrypt ACME HTTP-01 challenge validation paths.
steps_taken:
1. Confirmed cert expiry using 'openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 -servername api.example.com'.
2. Checked Cert-Manager CertificateRequest status: found failed HTTP01 challenge.
3. Whitelisted /.well-known/acme-challenge/ path in Nginx ingress configuration.
resolution: Switched Cert-Manager Issuer from HTTP-01 challenge to Route53 DNS-01 challenge to eliminate dependency on HTTP routing. Re-issued valid wildcard TLS certificate and set up 30-day proactive Slack alert.
